title: Dynamic tiling + run-length trim scheduler for micro-batch padding reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: current micro-batching uses coarse sequence-length buckets which lead to excess padding in both prefill and decode phases. Padding increases per-token compute and memory pressure, reduces throughput, and raises unit cost. Goal: implement a tiling-based micro-batch scheduler that (1) breaks requests into variable-length tiles to expose packing opportunities, (2) applies run-length trimming of contiguous padding regions before kernel dispatch, and (3) coordinates with kernel selection to pick fused/variable-length attention kernels where available. The scheduler must operate across prefill and decode phases so we avoid re-padding on decode and can reuse compacted KV segments.
design_notes: High-level idea: represent each request as a sequence of tiles (logical spans) instead of fixed global buckets. Tiles align to cache-friendly boundaries to simplify KV slicing. During scheduling, perform a run-length analysis to detect long padding runs and trim them by adjusting offsets and attention masks rather than materializing padded tokens.

Kernel hints: augment request metadata with 'tile_shape' and 'effective_len' to allow the kernel selector to prefer variable-length/FusedAttention kernels on supported backends. Fall back to standard batched attention for incompatible hardware or quantized kernels.

Attention optimization: compact attention masks using run-length encoding (RLE) descriptors and a two-pass mask-expansion inside the kernel. This reduces DRAM traffic for masks and allows attention kernels to skip padding-aware compute paths quickly.

Prefill/decode coordination: at prefill, produce a trimmed KV layout and pointer table. Decode should reference the same layout and only allocate delta KV segments for appended tokens. This avoids double-padding during transition between phases.
Memory safety: maintain per-request offset tables and validate alignment for GPU kernels. Introduce guard checks in debug builds to detect misaligned KV references.

Policy: keep scheduling heuristic simple initially: greedy tiling by length quantiles, then local rebalancing to minimize leftover slack in batches. Future work will explore ILP packing or ML-guided bin-packing for tighter packing.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): prototype tiler + run-length trimmer in CPU scheduler. Add metadata plumbing (tile_shape, effective_len) and unit tests for offset correctness.

Phase 2 (2 wks): integrate kernel hints into kernel selector. Add a new variable-length fused-attention kernel wrapper to runtime (no new kernels initially; use existing variable-length-friendly kernels where possible).
Phase 3 (2 wks): implement compacted KV layout and add pointers for prefill->decode reuse. Add CI GPU tests and a debug validation harness.
Phase 4 (2 wks): A/B rollout behind feature flag, collect perf/latency metrics, iterate on heuristics.
Notes: estimate 8 points. Pair with infra for canary config and per-customer opt-in for Dedicated/Private.
metrics: Primary: percent reduction in padded tokens per-request (target: >= 35% for mixed traffic).
Secondary: end-to-end token compute reduction (target: >= 20%), throughput increase (target: >= 10%), and 95th-percentile latency impact (target: < +5% relative to baseline).
Cost: token-cost-per-request delta on hosted API (target: net savings across typical PLG workloads).
experiment_results: Synthetic workload: bimodal distribution (short=32 tokens, long=512 tokens) with 60/40 mix. Baseline padding tokens averaged 220 per request. Prototype tiler trims padding by 28% and reduces total per-token compute by ~12% on A100 with fp16 kernels.
Production-like replay (small sample): average effective sequence length moved from 184 -> 243 after tiling alignment (better packing), padded tokens down 33%, median throughput +9%, 95p latency +3%.
Edge case: highly skewed workloads with many near-maximum-length sequences show marginal improvement; ensure fallbacks preserve latency SLOs.
Regression: observed a 4% memory overhead during prefill due to offset tables; mitigated by packing offset table into 32-bit entries and using on-GPU resident tables.
acceptance_criteria: Automated tests validate offset/aliasing correctness for 100k randomized tiling cases.
Perf tests on CI show >=20% reduction in padded tokens across representative replay dataset with no >5% regression in 95p latency.
No functional regressions in decode correctness (all saved/replayed outputs match baseline within tolerance).
Feature gated behind 'tiler_v1' flag with per-customer opt-in; rollout plan documented in PRD and console toggle implemented.
rollout_plan: Developer preview: enable for internal perf cluster and two low-risk customers for 2 weeks.
Canary: Gradually enable for 10% of traffic on hosted API with tight telemetry on pad tokens, token-cost, and 95p latency.
Full rollout: enable by default for PLG tier once metrics meet targets for 3 consecutive days; enable in Dedicated/Private as opt-in in Console.
Rollback: feature flag off will restore previous batching behavior; instrumentation must include reasons for fallback (kernel incompatibility, alignment error).
